sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

The claimant, being dissatisfied with the compensation of Rs.1,58,600/- awarded by the Tribunal,
is in appeal.

2. The fact that the accident occurred and the further fact that the offending vehicle was insured is not in dispute.
3.

The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence, has recorded a finding that the claimant has suffered the following injuries " Tenderness over the shaft of proximal 1/3rd right femur, knee, arc of movement of right hip, flexion restricted, movement of right knee restricted difficulty in climbing stairs, squatting, sitting crossed leg and kneeling."

4. The Tribunal has thereafter awarded the following sums as compensation:
 Sl. Amount  Particulars  No. in (Rs.)
 1. Loss of future income 1,20,000
2 . Medical expenses 28,600  3. Conveyance, food, nourishment, 10,000
attendant charges
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,20,000/- as lumpsum for loss of future income.
The counsel for the claimant therefore, contends that this award is improper having regard to the fact Sri Gowtham S vs Mr Shivashekara K S on 23 March, 2023

2 that the claimant was 16 years old and the multiplier ought to have adopted after assessing the permanent disability.
6. It cannot be in dispute that if the claimant is more than 15 years old, the Tribunal has applied the multiplier method after assessing the permanent disability.

7. It is not in dispute that the doctor, who was examined has stated that the whole body to the claimant, who was 16 yeas old was 12%.
8.
Karnataka State Legal Services Authority has fixed the income of Rs.9,500/- in respect of the accident of the year,2016.
9. As the claimant was aged 16 years, a multiplier of '18' would have to be applied.
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.2,46,240/- (Rs.9,500 x 12 x 18 x 12%) towards 'loss of future income'.
10. The Tribunal has not awarded any sums towards pain and suffering and loss of amenities.

Having regard to the length of hospitalization, percentage of disability and the injuries suffered by the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards 'pain and suffering'
and Rs.75,000/- towards loss of amenities.

11. Having regard to the length of the stay of the claimant in the hospital, the claimant would also be entitled to 'conveyance, food and nourishment and attendant charges' at Rs.40,000/- as against the sum of Rs.10,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

12. The sums awarded as medical expenses by the Tribunal, being based on documentary evidence,
does not call for modification and hence confirmed.

13. The claimant had suffered 12% disability and the evidence on record indicates that he has restriction in the movement of his lower limb and therefore, I am of the view that it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards marriage prospects.

14. Consequently the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.5,14,840/- as against Rs.1,58,600/-, along with interest from the date of petition till its realization.
16. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
17. The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at 6% per annum.
18. The claimant would not be entitled for the interest on the compensation for the delayed period of 389 days in filing the appeal.
19. The disbursement of the compensation amount shall be in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
20. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
